placements.title: Operational readiness as its own governed category
placements.frame: Does this content treat the organization's operational readiness (its capacity to actually execute recovery, rollback, or continuity actions) as a governed category with its own cadence and ownership, distinct from the systems or features it protects?

placements.title: A capability counts only once it is rehearsed on a schedule someone owns
placements.frame: Does this expression treat a recovery or continuity capability as real only when it is regularly rehearsed, scheduled, and assigned an accountable owner — rather than merely designed, documented, or assumed to exist?
placements.why: src-1 issues the directive establishing a monthly Atlas rollback rehearsal cadence; src-2 supplies the justifying principle that an unrehearsed rollback is effectively no rollback at all; src-3 restates the cadence as a ratified field; src-4 assigns an accountable owner. Together these are not a one-time fact but a recurring institutional practice — future envelopes (drill results, missed cadences, ownership handoffs) will keep feeding this same subject, which is why it clears the narrative grain test rather than sitting as a single fact under some other theme.
